description: An archived first-generation local object-store experiment with XOR sharding, versioned reads, quota placement and a partial Flask API.
scope_audience: The stated scope is a small educational/learning store whose internals are hand-built, not production or S3-compatible storage. README calls it the predecessor to myminio2, which moves the same idea across network backends.

creativity.reason: A locally interesting learning implementation combines quota-aware placement, time-based versions and single-parity repair; the README frames it as a hand-built MinIO-inspired experiment, not a novelty claim.

current_usefulness.reason: The EC core has a committed migration verification record for round-trip, lost-shard repair and version operations, but the HTTP layer has broken routes and writes RAID-0 through POST.

expected_usefulness.reason: As a finished educational prototype it can teach local parity and quota mechanics; the documented bespoke API and one-shard limit preclude a production-storage interpretation.

impl_progress.reason: Inspected EC.set/get/split/cat implement shard storage and reconstruction, and project-status records a prior bounded smoke check; the HTTP routes remain partially broken.

presentability.reason: README clearly distinguishes the unrelated stock MinIO compose setup from the custom store and candidly documents broken endpoints and deployment limits.

delivery_likelihood.reason: The archived educational core and its prior migration smoke evidence are present; no promise of a production API is made.

verification: README, ec4 implementation and committed project-status evidence; executed=false; Prior verification is documentary evidence, not reproduced here; network service and MinIO deployment were not run.

evidence.locator: lines 5-23, purpose and status; lines 85-127, HTTP/API and implemented operations

contribution: A compact, inspectable local-storage experiment that exposes parity math, placement and repair rather than wrapping MinIO. Its independent learning value is clearer than any claim to S3 behavior or production durability.
alternatives_question: Which educational local object-store implementations expose quota placement, point-in-time versions and XOR shard repair, and what part of that task remains meaningfully different here?
reason: The implementation and prior verification support retaining it as a learning artifact, while non-repetition and usefulness beyond that bounded audience require comparison.
next_step: For any public showcase, reproduce the EC smoke test in temporary directories and state plainly that the HTTP adapter and compose cluster are not the verified core.
